subject: Marketplace integration: request for full subprocessor manifest + geo-tagging
messages:
From: Samir Bose <samir@marketsquare.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request — full subprocessor manifest + geo-tagging for marketplace integration

Hi Mateo,

Hope you’re well. We’re close to finalizing our integration plan for the MarketSquare marketplace connector and legal/compliance needs a complete subprocessor manifest for Redwood that includes:

- canonical vendor name
- primary country of processing (geo-tag)
- whether the vendor is onshore-only (Y/N)
- data types processed (e.g., telemetry, pseudonymized logs, user content)
- any known cross-border transfer endpoints

We also need evidence where applicable (SOC 2 cover page, encryption-at-rest note, or a pointer to an export map) for processors handling tenant data or any customer content. Our security review team would like this by EOD next Wednesday (2026-12-07) to keep the integration timeline.

Can you provide the manifest or tell me the best contact to pull it from? If there are processors that are temporary/contractor-only, please flag them and indicate expected removal dates.

Thanks — I can loop in legal if that helps.

Samir
Procurement, MarketSquare

--
Attachment: none in this initial message

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request — full subprocessor manifest + geo-tagging for marketplace integration

Samir — thanks for the clear ask.

We can get that to you. I’m attaching our current subprocessor manifest (CSV export) that includes canonical name, primary processing country, and a short classification of data types. For the items you flagged (temporary processors, onshore-only), we’ve annotated the CSV with an "onshore_only" column and a "temporary_until" column where applicable.

Quick clarifications before we assemble evidence:
- Do you need SOC 2 attestations for all processors or only those that store or directly process customer-submitted content?
- When you say “cross-border transfer endpoints,” do you expect IP-level egress nodes (e.g., edge proxies/CDNs) listed separately from vendor headquarters? We can provide both but want to match your intake format.

We aim to get the manifest + initial evidence pointers in the next 48 hours. Kimberly (copied) will own gathering SOC2 extracts and the transfer map for any processors flagged as handling content. Lauren from Product Compliance is cc’d and can confirm scope.

Best,
Mateo
Partner Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: marketplace_subproc_manifest_v1.csv (csv)

Hi Samir / Mateo — Kim from Security & Compliance here. Thanks for the initial manifest — that helps. A few requests to make the package reviewable by MarketSquare’s security team: 

1) For any vendor marked as processing "user content" or "customer payloads", please provide a one-page extract showing: SOC 2 scope (if attested), encryption-in-transit & at-rest statements, and contact for security attestations (email).
2) For vendors flagged as having cross-border egress, we need a transfer map PDF showing the country-to-country hops for any tenant data (edge hops included). A simple table is fine.
3) If any subprocessor uses Redwood-managed KMS/HSM versus client-provided keys, flag that column explicitly.
4) Please confirm retention limits for telemetry/metrics vendors (max retention in days).

If MarketSquare prefers, we can create a minimal evidence bundle template you can fill (one-page per vendor) — I’ve created a Drive folder and shared the template: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cExampleSubprocEvidence

Timeline: We’re targeting to hand off a verified evidence bundle to MarketSquare legal by 2026-12-07. If you can provide SOC 2 extracts and any transfer maps by Thurs 12/3 EOD, that would be ideal.

Thanks — Kim
Senior Compliance Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachment: none (template is on Drive)
